quizzes.stem: A team tags 50,000 short support tickets overnight, each with one of eight categories. Speed per ticket is irrelevant, spend matters, and the categories are easy to tell apart. What is the best first step?

options.a: Begin with the lowest-priced tier and score it on genuine samples
options.b: Begin with Claude Opus 5.5, because the overview names it the usual starting point
options.c: Begin with the top tier, then step down if the budget complains
options.d: Send the first thousand to each tier and keep whichever bills least

explanation.a: Simple, high-volume, cost-sensitive work fits the efficiency-first path, validated on real data (the two strategies).
explanation.c: Ruled out because the capability-first path is "Suited to complex reasoning, accuracy that outweighs cost, and high-autonomy agent work", and this task is the opposite.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the efficiency-first path says to "Begin with the fast, low-cost tier, test thoroughly, and move up only for a gap you can name", and the overview's default is only a starting point for most workloads.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the decision rule is to "compare accuracy, quality and edge-case handling, then weigh cost", and a choice on price alone never checks the labels.

quizzes.stem: A coding agent running on the mid tier fails a handful of hard tasks each day. The team plans to move the entire system to the top tier. Which alternative should they try first?

options.a: Switch on fast mode for the hard tasks and compare the new results
options.b: Drop to the fastest tier and retry each failure several times
options.c: Run the difficult cases at higher effort and measure the change
options.d: Pin the id to a dated snapshot in case the model has drifted

explanation.c: The page says tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models, and a narrower change targets the hard tasks only.
explanation.a: Ruled out because fast mode offers "up to 2.5x higher output speed at premium pricing", which buys speed at a higher price, not more depth on hard tasks.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the cheapest model for everything under-serves exactly the cases that need depth", and retrying hard tasks on a weaker tier moves the wrong way.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "every Claude model id is a pinned snapshot", so the model behind a fixed id has not drifted and pinning it again adds no depth on hard tasks.

quizzes.stem: A marketing manager who does not write code wants weekly newsletters drafted in the house voice, using last quarter's issues as reference. An IT colleague offers to build whatever they need. Which approach fits best?

options.a: A cloud-platform deployment so the drafts stay inside the company account
options.b: A scheduled script that calls the Messages API weekly with the issues attached
options.c: A bespoke agent on the Agent SDK that reads the archive before each draft
options.d: A Project in the app holding the tone guide and earlier editions

explanation.d: A Project holds instructions and reference files for recurring non-developer work, and the colleague's offer does not change who does the work (the apps bullet and the first trap).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A recurring chat workflow for a non-developer does not need code", and "building an endpoint adds cost and maintenance for nothing".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the Agent SDK row is for "Developers building custom agents", and a Project already holds the archive without code.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table points "Security requires all traffic through the company's cloud account" to a cloud platform, and the scenario states no such rule.

quizzes.stem: A bank must run every model call under the identity and permission setup of the cloud provider that already hosts its servers. Developers still want the same Claude models from their own code. Which option fits?

options.a: Build on the Agent SDK and set its permission options there
options.b: Order access through that vendor's matching platform listing
options.c: Call the Messages API directly with rules in the system prompt
options.d: Send the calls to Claude Managed Agents and its hosted harness

explanation.b:
The table sends "Security requires all traffic through the company's cloud account" to a cloud platform,
   which adds its own identity and permission model while serving the same models.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the
   Agent SDK row is for "Developers building custom agents", and the scenario asks for no custom agent, only the
   cloud provider's identity setup.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "a cloud platform
   adds its own identity and permission model", while a system prompt only instructs the model.
explanation.d:
is ruled out
   because the managed agents row is for "Teams with long-running, asynchronous work", and the scenario describes
   no long-running job, only calls that must run under the provider's identity setup.

quizzes.stem: A developer wrote "answer in French" into a Project's instructions. Their own integration, calling the Messages API, still replies in English. What is the best explanation?

options.a: The Messages API supports fewer languages than the apps do
options.b: The integration needs the Agent SDK before it can follow language rules
options.c: French must be requested through a model parameter that the API leaves unset
options.d: Settings kept in the chat product are not sent with requests from code

explanation.d: Where instructions live decides where they are read, and a Project's instructions do not reach the API (the carry-across section and the third trap).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The model is the same family behind every door, so its capabilities and its quirks are the same".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the instruction lives "In the API, in the system prompt your code sends", and no model parameter is involved.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Instructions written for one place do not appear in another unless you put them there", and no other surface is a precondition.

quizzes.stem: A team's research job runs for hours with nobody watching: mostly routine page fetching and note-taking, with a few hard judgment calls. Which design fits?

options.a: Hand it to managed agents with cheap workers and one strong decider
options.b: Run it through the app's research feature with a Project for notes
options.c: Run the strongest tier through the Messages API on the team's own servers
options.d: Use the fastest tier for each step, then escalate only when the job fails

explanation.a: A job that runs for hours belongs in managed agents, and an orchestrator that hands bulk work to cheaper workers puts most tokens on the cheaper model while a stronger one takes the hard calls.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "An app has a person at every step", and nobody is watching this job.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the situation table points "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers" to managed agents.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page's executor "escalates hard decisions to an advisor", while a wrong judgment call does not make the job fail, so escalating on failure never sends the hard calls upward and leaves them with the model that "under-serves exactly the cases that need depth".

quizzes.stem: A feature must call one specific Claude model for two years. In review, someone flags the id hard-coded in the source. What is the most likely concern?

options.a: That snapshot has a retirement date, and nothing plans the move
options.b: Dated ids are rejected by the Messages API in favour of aliases
options.c: A shorter alias would follow new releases and should replace it
options.d: Hard-coded ids bypass the pinned snapshot, so replies drift between calls

explanation.a: The table shows retirement dates, and an id with a retirement date needs a migration plan before the date (the third trap).
explanation.d: Ruled out because "every Claude model id is a pinned snapshot", so replies do not drift under a fixed id.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "For Haiku 4.5 the dated id is the snapshot and the shorter name is an alias", so dated ids are accepted.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page counts "including the dateless IDs used from the 4.6 generation on" among the pinned snapshots, so an alias is no more of a tracker, and its advice is to "Pin ids in production and migrate on purpose".

quizzes.stem: A team's helper remembered the conversation when it ran in an app chat. Rebuilt on the Messages API, it answers every message as if it were the first. What is the fix?

options.a: Turn on the endpoint's stored-chat setting for the account
options.b: Add "remember our history" to the system prompt
options.c: Include the prior exchange in the body of each call
options.d: Copy the app's Project instructions into the new setup

explanation.c: Ownership of state decides where history lives: "The API keeps nothing; your code resends history", so each request must carry the earlier turns (the carry-across section).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The API keeps nothing", so no account setting stores the chat.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The API sends only what you put in the request", and a sentence in the system prompt carries no history.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the memory came from the app itself, since "An app keeps your conversation", and "Instructions written for one place do not appear in another unless you put them there" concerns instructions, which carry no earlier turns.

quizzes.stem: A team calls the same Claude model through the Claude API and through Amazon Bedrock, reusing one config file with a single name string for both. Both platforms list the model as current and access is granted, but Bedrock answers that the name is unknown. What is the most likely cause?

options.a: Bedrock runs a different generation of the family, so the name never matched
options.b: Each vendor gives the family its own id, so the value must differ
options.c: Cloud platforms expect a date-stamped snapshot name, not a plain one
options.d: The file holds the full id, while Bedrock accepts only the short alias

explanation.b: The cloud platforms bullet lists a separate id for each platform, for example anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "Same model family; different ids, access and sometimes features", so the generation is the same and only the id differs.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page's example "anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock" carries no date, and the dated form "claude-haiku-4-5@20251001 on Google Cloud" is one platform's own id.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the models overview "lists a separate id for each platform", and the page's example "anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock" is a Bedrock id of its own, not a short Claude API alias.
